chunks: Ibn Faḍḍāl, from ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mughīrah, who said:

I was Waqifī, and I performed hajj in that state. Then when I came to Makkah, something stirred in my chest, so I clung to al-Multazam. Then I said: O Allah, You have indeed known my seeking and my intention, so guide me to the best of religions. Then it occurred within me that I should go to al-Riḍā عليه السلام.

So I came to al-Madīnah and stood at his door, and I said to the servant: Tell your master that a man from the people of Iraq is at the door. He said: Then I heard his call while he was saying: Enter, O ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mughīrah, enter, O ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mughīrah. So I entered, and when he looked at me, he said to me: Allah has answered your supplication and guided you to His religion. So I said: I bear witness that you are the hujjah of Allah and His trustee over His creation.

key_terms.أَمِينُهُ: His trustee; one entrusted by Allah over creation
key_terms.إِرَادَتِي: my intention; his inward aim and resolve
key_terms.الْمُلْتَزَمِ: the place at the Kaʿbah where he clung in supplication
key_terms.حُجَّةُ اللَّهِ: the divine proof of Allah; a title affirming the Imam’s authority
key_terms.دُعَاءَكَ: your supplication; the prayer Allah answered
key_terms.دِينِهِ: His religion; the true religion to which he was guided
key_terms.طَلِبَتِي: my seeking; the spiritual quest he presented before Allah

ai.seo_question: How did ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mughīrah come to recognize Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام as the hujjah of Allah?
ai.summary: This narration recounts how ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mughīrah, while previously holding Waqifī beliefs, sought guidance from Allah at al-Multazam during hajj. He was inwardly directed to Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام, whose immediate recognition of him and response to his supplication led him to testify to the Imam’s divine authority.
